newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE cocoa resists selling pressure from New York.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE cocoa resists selling pressure from New York.

text.p: London cocoa futures staged fierce resistance to tumbling New York prices on Wednesday as most positions wiped out early losses and some even managed to record gains.
But abundant stocks in West Africa and a weakening nearby structure suggested gains could be difficult to sustain above 890 stg and 900 stg, traders said.
"There is a pretty dire situation on cocoa," said one trader. "The pound (sterling) is strong against the French franc. That's bringing in the origins."

Others said London held well in the afternoon as the key March contract recovered from a session low of 869 stg to end unchanged at 874 stg a tonne. May was up one at 897 while further forwards starting from Dec 1997 gained up to six stg on light trade buying linked to industry offtake.
"In the afternoon we held quite well considering the pressure from New York," said one trader.
Earlier prices drooped on origin offers in nearby contracts.
The day's turnover reached 6,702 lots, mostly involving structure deals around March whose spread to May weakened to 23-24 stg from 22 stg on Tuesday.
In fundamental news, Ivorian port sources said warehouses were swollen to their around 390,000-tonne capacity following small December shipments.
Some reckoned this was due to high bids in the automated auction system which may have prompted exporters to delay shipments in the hope of higher rates.
Warehouses were also filling up in Ghana's second port Takoradi.

Fund selling and origins dragged the CSCE March contract to a new low of $1,300 after prices gapped $10 down at the opening. The strength of the U.S. dollar against sterling was also weighing on the market through arbitrage sales.
